answer.reason: The verses tell of Ezra's coming to Jerusalem, his reading of the law to the people, and the oath to put away foreign wives.

clauses.english: came to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes
clauses.quote: he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month

clauses.english: brought the law before the people and read it from morning until midday
clauses.quote: he read therein before the street that was before the water gate

clauses.english: made the priests, the Levites and all Israel swear to put away their foreign wives
clauses.quote: made the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear

doubts: NEH 12:1, 12:13, 12:26, 12:33 and 12:36 only list Ezra among priests and processions and were left out.
The putting away of the foreign wives is cited only to the oath in EZR 10:5, since the later verses describe the people's examination rather than Ezra's own act.
